name: claim.vet
description: Access VA benefits faster with AI

faqs.q: How long does a VA disability claim take?
faqs.a: The average VA disability claim takes 100-150 days to process, though complex claims or those requiring a C&P exam can take longer. Using Claim.Vet to submit a fully developed claim (FDC) with all evidence upfront can significantly reduce processing time.

faqs.q: What is a VA disability rating and how is it calculated?
faqs.a: A VA disability rating is a percentage (0%-100%) assigned to each service-connected condition. The VA uses a combined ratings formula — not simple addition — to calculate your overall rating. For example, a veteran with two 50% ratings does not receive 100%; they receive approximately 75%.

faqs.q: What is a nexus letter for a VA claim?
faqs.a: A nexus letter is a medical opinion written by a licensed physician that establishes a connection (nexus) between your current medical condition and your military service. It is one of the most powerful pieces of evidence you can submit with a VA disability claim, especially for secondary conditions.

faqs.q: Am I eligible for VA benefits?
faqs.a: Most veterans who served on active duty and were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable are eligible for VA benefits. Eligibility for specific programs like disability compensation, VA home loans, and the GI Bill depends on your service history, discharge status, and medical conditions.

faqs.q: What should I do if my VA disability claim was denied?
faqs.a: If your VA claim is denied, you have three options: file a Supplemental Claim with new evidence (VA Form 20-0995), request a Higher-Level Review (VA Form 20-0996), or appeal to the Board of Veterans’ Appeals (VA Form 10182). You have one year from the denial date to respond.

faqs.q: How do I file a VA disability claim?
faqs.a: You can file a VA disability claim online at VA.gov, by mail, or in person at a regional VA office. To file online using Claim.Vet, our AI walks you through VA Form 21-526EZ step by step, helps you gather supporting evidence, and generates a ready-to-submit PDF — all for free.

faqs.q: What is FeedBug?
faqs.a: FeedBug is a visual bug reporting widget for teams using Linear. Your QA testers click on the bug directly on your website, FeedBug captures a screenshot, console logs, network errors and the HTML context, and creates a Linear ticket automatically.

faqs.q: How do I install FeedBug?
faqs.a: Add one script tag to your website (before the closing body tag). No SDK, no build step. Works with React, Vue, Next.js, Nuxt, Angular, Svelte, Rails or plain HTML. Takes about two minutes to set up.

faqs.q: How does FeedBug integrate with Linear?
faqs.a: You connect FeedBug to your Linear workspace via OAuth, choose the team and project where tickets should land, and every bug report becomes a Linear issue with the screenshot, diagnostics, and a link back to the live pin on the page. Tickets are attributed to the actual QA member who reported them.

faqs.q: Will FeedBug slow down my website?
faqs.a: No. The widget is around 10kb gzipped, loads asynchronously, and runs in a Shadow DOM so it never conflicts with your existing styles or scripts. It only loads on the domains you explicitly allow.

faqs.q: What is the MCP server for?
faqs.a: FeedBug ships an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server you can plug into Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf or VS Code. Your AI agent reads the Linear ticket, opens the exact file and line thanks to the captured HTML context, proposes the patch and opens the PR.

faqs.q: Is there a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes. The Free plan includes 1 project and 10 feedbacks per month, with screenshots, diagnostics and visual pins. Paid plans (Pro at 9€/month, Team at 19€/month) lift those limits and unlock the MCP server, session replay, webhooks and custom data capture. No credit card required to start.

faqs.a: The Free Fact Checker works with ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and any other LLM that you chat with in a browser.

faqs.a: The Free Fact Checker works on any site where you can highlight text in a browser. Try it on Facebook, X (Twitter), YouTube, Instagram, Bluesky, Reddit, and major news sites.

faqs.a: The Free Fact Checker requires permission to read and change data on the website https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com. This is the URL for the Google Gemini server that the Free Fact Checker calls when you trigger it.

faqs.q: Why should I use this?
faqs.a: LLMs lie. People lie. It's hard to know what to believe online. Manually verifying everything is basically impossible. The Free Fact Checker makes that quicker and easier by grounding every check in Google Search results.

faqs.a: The Free Fact Checker uses Google Search to find information. To the degree that you trust Google Search, you can trust this. It will never give you an AI's opinion — only search-grounded answers. You should always look at the citations to see if they're trustworthy.

faqs.q: Is it really free?
faqs.a: Yes. The extension is free and you can get a free Gemini API Key from Google. Google lets you make 20 grounding requests per day on the free plan. If you want more requests per day or want to use a different Gemini model, you will need to set up billing in AI Studio.

faqs.q: What is AI pentesting and how does it work?
faqs.a: AI pentesting uses autonomous agents to simulate real-world attacks against your applications, APIs, and infrastructure. The agents map your attack surface, probe for vulnerabilities, attempt exploitation, and validate findings — all without manual intervention.

faqs.q: How long does a pentest take?
faqs.a: Most pentests complete within hours rather than the weeks typically required for traditional manual engagements. You can monitor agent activity in real time and receive your full report the same day.

faqs.q: What's the difference between white-box and black-box testing?
faqs.a: In white-box testing, agents have access to your source code and can identify vulnerabilities through code analysis alongside active probing. Black-box testing simulates an external attacker with no internal knowledge. Maced supports both modes — white-box testing is enabled automatically when you connect your reposito

faqs.q: Do I need to share my source code?
faqs.a: No — source code access is optional. Black-box pentests run without it. However, connecting your repos enables white-box analysis, which significantly increases coverage by allowing agents to understand application logic, authentication flows, and data models.

faqs.q: How do you prevent false positives?
faqs.a: Every finding is validated through actual exploitation against your live target. If an agent cannot successfully exploit and confirm a vulnerability, it is discarded. Only verified, reproducible findings appear in your report.

name: OpenSourceAIHub
description: Stop AI data leaks and control spend.

faqs.q: What is OpenSourceAIHub in plain English?
faqs.a: It’s a security layer that sits between your app and AI companies like OpenAI, Groq, or Mistral. When your app sends a message to AI, the Hub checks it first — removes any sensitive data (like emails, passwords, or credit card numbers), selects the most cost-efficient available provider, and then forwards the cleaned m

faqs.q: Does the Hub store my data?
faqs.a: No. We only log metadata (like "1 email address was blocked") — we never store the actual content of your messages or the AI’s responses. Your data passes through our security layer and is forwarded to the AI provider. Nothing is saved on our servers.

faqs.q: Is this compatible with my existing code?
faqs.a: If your app uses the OpenAI SDK (the most popular AI library), you only need to change two lines: the API key and the base URL. Everything else — your models, your prompts, your response handling — stays exactly the same.

faqs.q: What does "BYOK" mean?
faqs.a: BYOK stands for "Bring Your Own Key." It means you already have an account (and API key) with a provider like OpenAI, Google Gemini, xAI, Groq, or Together.ai. On the Pro plan, you save those keys in the Hub, and we use them to make AI calls on your behalf — so you pay the provider directly at their regular price with

faqs.q: What if I don’t have my own API keys?
faqs.a: That’s perfectly fine! The "Managed Credits" plan is designed exactly for this. Add credits to your Hub wallet (10M Credits / $10 minimum), and we handle everything — we use our own provider accounts to process your requests.

faqs.q: Do I need to configure DLP rules before my data is protected?
faqs.a: No. Every request is protected from your very first API call. The Hub applies a "Maximum Protection" default policy that scans for all 28 entity types (emails, credit cards, SSNs, API keys, prompt injection attacks, and more) and redacts any matches before the AI model sees them.

faqs.q: What is a Peppol validator?
faqs.a: A Peppol validator checks whether a UBL XML invoice complies with Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 and EN16931 business rules. It runs schematron-based checks for schema issues, missing fields, invalid identifiers, and rule violations.

faqs.q: What is an e-invoice?
faqs.a: An electronic invoice (e-invoice) is a structured digital document exchanged directly between seller and buyer systems, not a PDF or scanned image. In Europe, e-invoices follow the EN16931 standard and are typically encoded as UBL 2.1 XML. They can be validated, processed, and booked automatically without manual data e

faqs.q: How do I validate EN16931 invoices?
faqs.a: Upload your UBL XML invoice above and run validation against EN16931 and Peppol BIS schematron rules. Errors and warnings are shown inline with rule references. For CII / Factur-X invoices, use our Factur-X validator.

faqs.q: What is UBL 2.1 and how does it relate to Peppol?
faqs.a: UBL (Universal Business Language) 2.1 is the OASIS XML standard that defines the data format for invoices and credit notes. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is a profile built on top of UBL 2.1 that restricts and extends it with specific business rules for the Peppol network. EN16931 sits in between as the European semantic stan

faqs.q: What causes Peppol validation errors?
faqs.a: Common causes include missing mandatory fields (like seller/buyer identifiers or tax breakdowns), incorrect InvoiceTypeCode (BT-3), scheme ID mismatches on electronic addresses (PEPPOL-EN16931-R004), empty XML elements (PEPPOL-EN16931-R008), and calculation mismatches on line or document totals (BR-CO rules).

faqs.q: Can I validate Peppol credit notes?
faqs.a: Yes. Upload a UBL CreditNote XML file and it will be validated against the same Peppol BIS 3.0 and EN16931 rules. Peppol supports two approaches: a dedicated CreditNote document (code 381, positive amounts) or a negative Invoice (code 380, negative amounts). Both are valid.

faqs.a: The RAADS R Test can be useful as a structured screening aid, but it is not a diagnosis. faqs.a: The test has 80 statements scored across four domains. Your total RAADS R Test score is the sum of item scores, while domain scores show which areas contributed most to the result.

faqs.a: The RAADS R Test score range is 0 to 240. Higher scores usually mean stronger endorsement of traits measured by the screening tool, but a score should not be read as a diagnosis by itself.

faqs.a: Scores around 99 or 105 fall in the range often described as some autistic traits. They may be worth reflecting on or discussing with a clinician, but the exact meaning depends on your history, current context, and domain scores.

faqs.q: How do I identify a rock I found?
faqs.a: Photograph it in natural light on a plain background. Upload the image to an AI rock identifier. The AI checks color, luster, grain size, and crystal habit against a database of known rock types. Wet the surface first for better accuracy.

faqs.q: What are the three types of rocks?
faqs.a: Igneous (cooled from magma), sedimentary (compressed layers of sediment), and metamorphic (transformed by heat and pressure). Granite is igneous, sandstone is sedimentary, marble is metamorphic.

faqs.q: Is there a free rock identifier app?
faqs.a: Yes. Rock Identifier is free on iOS and Android. The web tool provides one free scan per day.

faqs.q: How accurate is AI rock identification?
faqs.a: High for common specimens like granite, quartz, basalt, and limestone. Lower for heavily weathered, mud-covered, or matrix-embedded surfaces. Some minerals require physical tests a camera cannot perform.

faqs.q: Can it tell me if my rock is valuable?
faqs.a: It provides the mineral name and a general value range. Actual value depends on size, quality, rarity, and demand. For gem-grade specimens, consult a gemologist.

faqs.q: What is the Mohs hardness scale?
faqs.a: A 1-to-10 ranking of scratch resistance. Talc is 1, diamond is 10. If your specimen scratches glass, it is at least Mohs 6.

faqs.q: How do credits work?+

faqs.a: It means you get the senior technical judgment a non-technical founder is usually missing, without hiring a full-time CTO. Will the architecture hold, is it secure, does it scale, repair or rebuild. AI writes the code, but someone has to own those decisions. That is the part I take.

faqs.q: Do I need to be technical to work with you?
faqs.a: No. If you know your business and can point at where it hurts, that is enough. The AI tools are good enough now that the biggest leverage is in the right judgment, not in you learning to code. My job is to build the technical bridge so you can stay with your business.

faqs.q: How does it start and what does it cost?
faqs.a: It starts with a 60-minute reality-check for 99 EUR. Not a sales pitch: you walk me through what you built and where it wobbles, I give you an honest read on repair-or-rebuild and what it would take. If the hour gives you nothing, you get your money back, no questions. Project pricing depends on scope and we set it clearly up front.

faqs.q: Do you only rescue prototypes, or do you build from scratch too?
faqs.a: Both. I meet you where you stand: a running prototype, a spec, or an idea worth sharpening. faqs.q: What is the difference between VARA, ADGM, DFSA, and CBUAE?
faqs.a: VARA regulates Dubai mainland VA activity (outside DIFC). ADGM/FSRA is the regulator of Abu Dhabi Global Market — a common law free zone that was first globally with a VA framework in 2018. faqs.a: Yes. You can download transcripts from entire YouTube channels or playlists in bulk. A channel with 1000 videos typically takes about 1 to 2 minutes to process.

faqs.q: What is a credit and how many do I need?
faqs.a: A credit is consumed for each video transcript you extract. For example, if you extract transcripts from a channel with 50 videos, you will use 50 credits. Credits never expire, and you get 10 free credits to start.

faqs.q: How accurate are the YouTube transcripts?
faqs.a: The accuracy depends on the quality of the original captions. For videos with professional captions, the accuracy is very high. For auto-generated captions, the accuracy varies based on factors like audio quality, accents, and background noise.

faqs.q: Do I need a YouTube API key or account?
faqs.a: No. You do not need to provide an API key or link your YouTube account. Just paste a video, channel, or playlist URL and start downloading transcripts.

faqs.q: How long does it take to extract transcripts?
faqs.a: For single videos, extraction is almost instant. For channels or playlists, the time depends on the number of videos. A channel with 1000 videos typically takes about 1-2 minutes to process.
